Q: Generate automatic SQL reports and output them to Google sheets A:

Disclosure: I built SaturnSQL, so I'm biased.

SaturnSQL does this without Apps Script: save the query, set a schedule, pick a Google Sheet as the destination. It connects to SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL, Redshift, ClickHouse and BigQuery. https://saturnsql.com/use-cases/sql-to-google-sheets

If it's genuinely a custom DBMS, the accepted answer is the right approach. Just note Apps Script caps execution at 6 minutes, so aggregate in SQL rather than pulling a raw extract.

Q: Why does .NET need IDisposable when destructors (finalizers) exist? What CLR internals make finalizers slow? A:

A finalizer is not simply another way of writing Dispose(). It changes how the GC has to manage the object's lifetime.

1. Finalizable objects cannot be reclaimed immediately

When the GC discovers that a normal object is unreachable, it can reclaim it during that collection.

For a finalizable object, the CLR first places the object into an internal finalization queue. The finalizer must execute before the object can finally be reclaimed.

Microsoft documents this behavior explicitly:

"The garbage collector adds an entry for each instance of the type to an internal structure called the finalization queue."

Object.Finalize Microsoft Learn

This means a finalizable object generally requires additional work and at least another opportunity for GC to reclaim its memory.

2. This can cause otherwise short-lived objects to survive collections

Generational GC is optimized around the assumption that most objects die young.

Normally, a short-lived object can be allocated in Gen0 and reclaimed in the next Gen0 collection.

A finalizable object, however, has to remain alive until its finalizer has run. If it survives a collection, it can be promoted to Gen1 and eventually Gen2.

It is worth being precise here: finalizable objects are not simply allocated directly into Gen2. The problem is that finalization can cause them to survive collections that they otherwise would have died in.

Microsoft documents the promotion rules here:

Fundamentals of garbage collection Microsoft Learn

3. Finalization is asynchronous

Finalizers do not run on the application thread that made the object unreachable. The CLR has a dedicated finalization mechanism/thread that executes pending finalizers.

This introduces another stage between "object is unreachable" and "memory can be reclaimed."

It also means that finalizer execution is nondeterministic. Microsoft explicitly states that the exact time at which a finalizer executes is undefined.

Object.Finalize Microsoft Learn

A problematic finalizer can therefore affect other objects waiting for finalization. Microsoft even warns that if a finalizer blocks indefinitely, other finalizers might never execute.

4. IDisposable avoids the finalization mechanism

With:

public sealed class FileHolder : IDisposable
{
    private readonly FileStream _stream;

    public FileHolder(string path)
    {
        _stream = new FileStream(path, FileMode.Open);
    }

    public void Dispose()
    {
        _stream.Dispose();
    }
}

Dispose() can release the file handle immediately.

The object itself can then be collected normally by the generational GC. It does not need to enter the finalization queue and does not need a finalizer thread to release the resource.

This is the fundamental reason IDisposable exists: GC manages managed memory; Dispose() manages resources whose lifetime needs to be deterministic.

Dispose Pattern Microsoft Learn

5. Why SafeHandle instead of writing finalizers everywhere?

SafeHandle provides a specialized and safer place for finalization of unmanaged handles.

Instead of:

~FileHolder()
{
    _stream.Dispose();
}

the recommended design is generally to let a SafeHandle own the native handle and rely on its carefully implemented finalization behavior as a last-resort fallback.

Microsoft explicitly recommends SafeHandle for unmanaged handles:

Implement a Dispose method Microsoft Learn

This is important because finalizers are difficult to implement correctly. During finalization, you cannot generally assume that other managed objects are still in a normal usable state.

In short

The cost of finalizers is not merely that "running a method is slow." The important CLR-level cost is that finalization changes the object's lifetime and GC processing:

  • The object must be tracked by the finalization mechanism.

  • It cannot be reclaimed immediately when first found unreachable.

  • It may survive collections and therefore be promoted to older generations.

  • Its cleanup executes asynchronously through the finalization mechanism.

  • A problematic finalizer can delay other finalizers.

  • Resource release becomes nondeterministic.

Therefore the usual pattern is:

IDisposable for deterministic cleanup, and SafeHandle/finalization as a last-resort safety net for unmanaged resources.

That's why the CLR has both mechanisms: they solve two different lifetime problems rather than being two equivalent ways of doing cleanup.

Q: converting dates into different format gives invalid date error A:

transform need a Date object (or a string)

So you can do so "bizarro" like

this._datePipe.transform(
   new Date("19/05/2020".split('/').reverse().join('-')), 
  'yyyy-MM-dd');

Well, really you can use directly the function formatDate

import {formatDate} from '@angular/common'
formatDate(
   new Date("19/05/2020".split('/').reverse().join('-')), 
  'yyyy-MM-dd','en-US');

That allow a simple string in ISO date format (yyyy-MM-dd)

formatDate(
   "19/05/2020".split('/').reverse().join('-'), 
  'yyyy-MM-dd','en-US');

Q: NetUserChangePassword 1351 error issue and NetUserSetInfo(with DPAPI) inquiry A:

DPAPI access problem may be related to your dll being hosted by LogonUI.exe, when you call NetUserChangePassword (with a correct domain, to avoid error 1351) the user profile is not yet loaded, so the password gets updated but DPAPI re-encryption of the master key fails.

This is just a theory. If you found a way around this problem, can you share your findings? I'm struggling with a similar problem.
